items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-07-21
items.q: Now he and Mel Ott, Wesley Barrow, and Chester Stamps, they all used to work out in an empty lot way back on the far side of Grettona about 75 years ago.

ctx.x: Now the Algiers, okay, you have to back up. What was this?

It was Sandlot Baseball. Was it organized in any way? Well it was semi-organized. Because first I started playing with the Gretton All-Stars. It was a fellow by the name of Wesley Barrow who later became general manager of the Baltimore Eli Giants back in the 50s. And Wesley Barrow came out of Franklin, Louisiana. But he was a hefty man. But he had something like a YMCA, a USO, or whatever you want to call it. He always kept young people together. People like J.B. Spencer who also went to the Homestead Grays. And…
Now what were the professional black teams that played in this area? What did New Orleans have the professional black teams?
